questions.question_text: Seven colleges J, K, L, M, N, O and P use Dell, Lenovo and HP systems; at least two colleges use each brand. K uses HP; M uses Lenovo; L uses Dell. N uses the same brand as P. Neither O nor N uses Dell. P does not use the same brand as M. Which brand does O use?
questions.explanation: N and P share a non-Dell brand, and P cannot use Lenovo because M does. Thus N and P are HP. With K also HP, and L already Dell, the remaining groups are Dell {L,J}, Lenovo {M,O}, HP {K,N,P}; O uses Lenovo.
questions.source: Tabular Puzzles 01 _ Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 4, Q1; brand table

questions.question_text: Nine persons L, M, N, O, P, Q, R, S and T study Marketing, Accounting and Architecture. Each course has two to four students. L studies with N, who studies neither Architecture nor Marketing. M and N study different courses. Q studies with neither L nor M. Marketing has one more student than Architecture. T studies with only one other person. O and S study the same course, but not with L. Q does not study with T. Who among the following studies Marketing?

options.B: The one who studies with P
options.D: The one who studies with O

questions.explanation: The course-size and clue constraints force course sizes Accounting=4, Marketing=3 and Architecture=2. L,N are Accounting; O,S are Marketing; T and M are Architecture; Q must be Marketing. Thus O’s study partners Q and S are in Marketing, making option D the only true choice among the listed descriptions.
questions.source: Tabular Puzzles 01 _ Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 7, Q2; course table

questions.question_text: Nine persons A-I applied for TNPSC, Railways and IBPS; each exam has two to four applicants. B and D applied for different exams, neither IBPS. A and F applied for the same exam. F applied for neither TNPSC nor Railways. The TNPSC count is one fewer than IBPS. H is in an exam group with only one other person and is not in Railways. E and I applied for the same exam. C and E applied for different exams. I and D applied for different exams. Who applied for IBPS?
questions.explanation: The unique assignment has IBPS {A,C,F}, TNPSC {D,H} and Railways {B,E,G,I}. Among the options only A and C are both IBPS applicants.
questions.source: Tabular Puzzles 01 _ Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 12, Q3; exam table

questions.question_text: Nine persons A-I wear Gold, Platinum or Diamond rings. D wears Diamond; C wears a different type from D. Only B shares H’s ring type. A and G share a type; neither D nor E shares A’s type. Exactly three people wear Diamond. F wears neither Gold nor Diamond. Who wears a Platinum ring?

options.A: The person sharing B’s ring type
options.C: The person sharing A’s ring type

questions.explanation: The unique ring groups are Gold {B,H}, Platinum {A,C,F,G} and Diamond {D,E,I}. F and the people sharing A’s type are Platinum, so both (b) and (c) are correct.
questions.source: Tabular Puzzles 01 _ Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 15, Q4; ring table

questions.question_text: Nine persons A-I receive distinct consecutive multiples of 50, all above 200 and below 700. I earns 350 more than B. Equal numbers of people earn more and less than G. H earns immediately less than I and 200 more than A. H’s wage equals B plus D; D earns 100 less than F. E earns more than C. Who earns the highest wage?

options.D: The person earning 250 more than I

questions.explanation: Enumeration over the nine consecutive wages yields A350, B250, C500, D300, E650, F400, G450, H550 and I600. E has the highest wage, 650.
questions.source: Tabular Puzzles 02  Class Notes.pdf, physical pp. 4-6, Q1; wages table

questions.question_text: Five students Q, O, N, I and H study at JNU, BHU, LNMU, AU and DU, and like Puma, Reebok, Nike, Sparx and Adidas, each once. H likes Adidas and is not at BHU. Q studies at DU and likes neither Puma nor Nike. N likes Reebok and is neither at BHU nor AU. O likes Nike. I is neither at JNU nor BHU. The LNMU student likes Puma. Which brand does Q like?
questions.explanation: N must be at JNU; I is then at LNMU and likes Puma. H is at AU with Adidas; O is at BHU with Nike. Q therefore likes Sparx, option B.
questions.source: Tabular Puzzles 02  Class Notes.pdf, physical pp. 7-8, Q2; university-brand table

questions.question_text: P, Q, R, S, T, U and V watch different movies Pokemon, Ad Astra, Toy Story, Aladdin, Frozen 2, Wonder Women and Rocketman in different cities Nasik, Agra, Bhopal, Rajkot, Jaipur, Pune and Surat. T is in Bhopal; U watches Toy Story; P is neither in Rajkot nor Nasik; T watches Aladdin; either S or V is in Agra; S and U are not in Nasik; P and V watch Pokemon and Ad Astra respectively; Q does not watch Rocketman; the Pune viewer watches neither Pokemon nor Toy Story; S and V are not in Pune; Frozen 2 is watched in Jaipur; neither Q nor S watches Frozen 2. Which pair does not belong?
questions.explanation: There are 12 valid arrangements, but the answer is invariant: V is never in Jaipur. Each of the first four listed pairs occurs in at least one valid arrangement, so only V–Jaipur is always the odd pair.
questions.source: Tabular Puzzles 02  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 10, Q3; city/movie table

questions.question_text: Seven persons A-G like distinct places Jama Masjid, Qutub Minar, Akshardham, Red Fort, Lotus Temple, India Gate and Jantar Mantar and belong to Delhi, Lucknow, Surat, Chennai, Shimla, Kanpur and Indore. C is from Indore but does not like Lotus Temple. The Kanpur person likes Jantar Mantar. B is from Lucknow and likes India Gate. G likes Akshardham but is not from Shimla. Neither A nor G is from Chennai. The Surat person likes Jama Masjid. E likes Qutub Minar. F likes neither Jama Masjid nor Jantar Mantar. The Lotus Temple person is not from Shimla. D is not from Surat. What place does the person from Chennai like?
questions.explanation: The unique assignment is A Surat–Jama Masjid, B Lucknow–India Gate, C Indore–Red Fort, D Kanpur–Jantar Mantar, E Shimla–Qutub Minar, F Chennai–Lotus Temple and G Delhi–Akshardham. The Chennai person therefore likes Lotus Temple, option C.
questions.source: Tabular Puzzles 02  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 14, Q4; city/monument table

questions.question_text: Seven persons A-G bought distinct shirts Allen Solly, Levis, Tommy Hilfiger, Parx, Raymond, Ajio and Peter England, and cars Honda, Suzuki, Ford, Jaguar, Fiat, Acura and Hyundai. E bought Parx; C has Acura. The Ford owner bought Tommy Hilfiger. Neither B nor G has Ford. Either G or B bought Levis. The Peter England buyer has Hyundai. Neither F nor G has Hyundai. Neither D nor A bought Peter England. The Levis buyer has neither Jaguar nor Honda. The Acura buyer did not buy Raymond. The Honda buyer has neither Raymond nor Parx. F does not have Honda. Neither E nor F has Fiat. Which combination is true?
questions.explanation: There are four valid assignments; in each, the Levis wearer has Suzuki. The other listed combinations are false in the verified solution set, making D invariant.
questions.source: Tabular Puzzles 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 4, Q1; shirt/car table

questions.question_text: Seven persons P, Q, R, S, T, U and V buy distinct fruits Mango, Plum, Kiwi, Fig, Apricot, Papaya and Peach at distinct weights 2-8 kg. Q buys Papaya weighing 6 kg; U’s fruit weighs 7 kg. Either T or R buys Plum. R’s fruit weighs twice Peach’s weight. Apricot is lightest. R and S have even weights. Kiwi is heavier than Fig. Neither S nor T buys Apricot. Mango weighs one kg more than Apricot. V buys neither Mango nor Peach. Plum weighs less than Kiwi. Who buys Peach?
questions.explanation: The unique table is P Mango/3 kg, Q Papaya/6 kg, R Kiwi/8 kg, S Peach/4 kg, T Plum/5 kg, U Fig/7 kg and V Apricot/2 kg. S buys Peach.
questions.source: Tabular Puzzles 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 8, Q2; fruit/weight table
